properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 29 at 3:38PM AKDT until October 30 at 4:15PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by
excessive rainfall is possible.


* WHERE...Seward.

* WHEN...Until 415 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Light rainfall will gradually increase in intensity this evening
and continue through Friday morning before the rain slowly tapers
off Friday afternoon. Rainfall rates of up to a quarter of an
inch per hour are possible between 10 PM tonight and 10 AM
Friday, with a storm total between 3 and 4 inches of rain likely
with this event. Prolonged heavy rain may lead to areas of
flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in low-lying and poor
drainage areas, and ponding of water on roadways.


- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.title: Tornado Warning issued October 29 at 6:35PM CDT until October 29 at 7:15PM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
At 634 PM CDT, a confirmed tornado was located near Cline, or 19
miles east of Brackettville, moving northwest at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Damaging tornado.

SOURCE...Radar confirmed tornado.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

Locations impacted include...
Turkey Mountain.
properties.instruction:
To repeat, a tornado is on the ground. TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a
basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy
building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in
a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect
yourself from flying debris.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 29 at 3:48PM CDT until October 29 at 6:45PM CDT by NWS San Angelo TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Sterling County in west central Texas...

* WHEN...Until 645 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 345 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain showers. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory
area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northwestern Sterling County.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 29 at 9:16AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor and Deland affecting Lake and Volusia
Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds and downstream tidal effects on the St
John River are slowing flow at Astor, which is also impacting river
levels upstream.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland, Astor...Minor to Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast to continue.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Thursday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...At Astor, river levels are forecast to slowly decline
but remain in Moderate Flood Stage for at least the next couple
weeks. Additional rises are possible as onshore winds
periodically increase.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 1215 AM EDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 6:40PM MDT until October 29 at 6:45PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...South Central Socorro County in central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 645 PM MDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 638 PM MDT, emergency management reported flooding in the
warned area. Flooding is already occurring.
- Flooding was reported in Socorro County in the Escondida and
Pueblito Communities. Several roads have been rendered impassible
near San Pedro.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Socorro, San Antonio, Bosque Del Apache Refuge, Escondida,
Lemitar, San Acacia, Laborcita, Luis Lopez and Chamizal.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
